title: Cameraman Wins $44,000: Salameh gives mother GTA 6 winnings; survives 60-minute robbery mission
text:
A video game robbery rarely leads to a life-changing moment outside the screen. However, MrBeast found a way to make it happen. The YouTube star offered real cash for every dollar his longtime cameraman, Tareq Salameh, could steal in GTA 6. What began as a race against police, security guards and a ticking clock soon became a personal mission. Salameh wanted to use the opportunity to give something back to his mother. After an intense 60-minute challenge, he walked away with approximately $44,000 for her, turning a gaming stunt into an emotional family moment.
Tareq Salameh fights setbacks in MrBeast’s GTA 6 challenge
The challenge featured in MrBeast Gaming's November 20 video, titled 'Whatever You Steal in GTA 6, You Keep!' The timing also added to the excitement, as the video arrived just one day after Rockstar Games released GTA 6.
Salameh entered the challenge with one clear goal. He wanted to earn as much as possible for his mother, who had supported him throughout his life.
'I'm, like, literally not joking. I'm doing this for my mom. I don't care how high it is,' he said.
Salameh, who was born in Saudi Arabia to Palestinian-Jordanian parents, moved to the United States as a child. He credited his mother with helping him adjust to his new surroundings, including teaching him English.
'She taught me everything. She taught me how to speak English. You know what I mean? I love my mom,' he said.
However, the challenge came with strict conditions. Every dollar stolen in GTA 6 counted towards the real-life payout, but getting arrested or killed would erase his entire balance. He also could not deposit his money in a bank to protect it.
His final task was equally difficult. He had to get aboard an aircraft and take off before the 60-minute timer expired.
MrBeast’s $44,000 GTA 6 challenge ends with an emotional payoff
Salameh initially built a strong balance by robbing a jewellery store, collecting more than $5,000. However, an attempted robbery at a loan store in Little Cuba nearly ended his chances. Armed security guards killed his character, wiping out everything he had earned.
Instead of giving up, he returned to the challenge and started building his total again. He stole vehicles, sold them for cash, broke into a Fleeca bank vault and targeted more businesses.
Eventually, his earnings crossed $44,000. But the biggest obstacle was still ahead.
With police chasing him and time running out, Salameh hijacked a bus at the airport and rushed towards a passenger aircraft. MrBeast urged him to forget about earning more money and focus on escaping before the deadline.
Salameh managed to get airborne just in time, securing the promised payout. His mother's reaction made the achievement even more meaningful, as she called him 'the best son ever'.
While the video also featured a promotion for financial technology platform Step, the challenge's emotional centre remained Salameh's decision to use his gaming skills to reward the person who had done so much for him.
For him, the biggest win was never the money inside GTA 6. It was the chance to give his mother a real $44,000 surprise.

title: Watch: Russian warship bursts into flames in suspected Ukraine drone attack in Libya
text:
A suspected Ukrainian sea drone attack struck a Russian navy warship at the port of Benghazi in eastern Libya, triggering an explosion and fire and leaving the vessel partially submerged.
The ship, identified as the Russian corvette Merkury, was docked at the port to refuel and take on supplies under a cooperation agreement between Moscow and the eastern-based Libyan administration. Satellite imagery shared by imagery provider Vantor showed that most of the vessel had capsized and sunk, with only its bow visible above water. Smoke and debris were also seen around the ship.
Two Libyan military officials told the Associated Press that Ukrainian sea drones had been launched at the warship from a base operated by Ukrainian forces in western Libya. At least four drones were intercepted, while two struck the vessel, they said. Neither Ukraine nor Russia has commented on the attack.
Meanwhile, local sources told Al Jazeera that an unknown number of Libyan and Russian nationals were killed. They also claimed the vessel was carrying weapons, ammunition and drones. Residents reportedly saw three drones attack the ship. These claims have not been publicly confirmed.
The eastern-based Libyan administration said the fire had been brought under control and launched a joint investigation with Russia to establish the source of the attack. It condemned the suspected strike as a violation of Libya's sovereignty and a threat to maritime safety.
"The Libyan government will not allow Libyan ports, territory or territorial waters to be turned into an arena for settling scores or exporting international conflicts," it said, adding that Libya was "not a party to the Russian-Ukrainian war".
Earlier, in a separate incident on Sunday evening, a sea drone struck a Malta-flagged commercial vessel off Benghazi. The eastern administration's Health Ministry said all crew members injured in the attack had been rescued and were receiving treatment. Almasar television reported that naval and air forces destroyed at least 12 other sea drones off the Mediterranean city.
The western-based Libyan government also expressed concern over attempts to involve the country's ports and civilian facilities in external conflicts.
Ukraine's 'presence' in Libya
The suspected attack comes amid reports of Ukrainian military and intelligence personnel operating in western Libya. Middle East security and defence expert Tallha Abdulrazaq told Al Jazeera that Ukrainian intelligence services were most likely behind the strike.
"There was a lot of reporting on the tail end of last year about there being a deal between the Ukrainian intelligence services and the Tripolitan government to establish a Ukrainian military and intelligence presence there," he said.
"In exchange, the Tripoli government would get Ukrainian military expertise," he added.
Libya has remained divided between rival administrations since a NATO-backed uprising toppled longtime leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011. A UN-recognised government is based in Tripoli, while a rival administration controls the east.
The head of the eastern-based Libyan government, Osama Hammad, has sought an international investigation, asking the UN to examine whether the drones were launched from western Libya and verify reports of Ukrainian experts operating in the country.

title: Wife's support during husband's medical training becomes key in divorce asset battle
text:
An Alabama appeals court has overturned part of a divorce settlement after finding that a lower court wrongly excluded a surgeon's medical-business investments from the couple's marital assets. The woman had worked and helped meet household expenses while her husband completed medical training. The case has now been sent back for a fresh assessment of the couple's property.
Sarah Gordon and Charles Gordon married in 2011, the year Charles completed medical school. He subsequently underwent an internship, a five-year orthopaedic surgery residency and a spine-surgery fellowship. During this period, Sarah worked as a nanny and took up other jobs to help pay household expenses.
Charles completed his fellowship in 2018, after which the couple moved to Baldwin County. He joined Baldwin Bone and Joint, an orthopaedic practice, and became a partner in 2020 or 2021 after borrowing money from First Horizon Bank. Sarah, meanwhile, became a full-time homemaker and had no separate income.
In its November 20, decision, the Alabama Court of Civil Appeals 
ruled
 that the husband's business interests should have been considered marital property. 
It reversed the property division and directed the lower court to determine their value and reconsider the distribution. However, it did not specify what share Sarah should receive.
Financial disputes during divorce
Sarah filed for divorce in February 2024. The trial court subsequently ordered the couple to maintain their existing financial arrangements and prohibited them from disposing of assets acquired during the marriage without permission.
Sarah later accused Charles of restricting her access to bank accounts and credit cards. She also alleged that he had withdrawn around $183,000 from their joint checking account.
Under a temporary agreement adopted by the court in October 2024, Charles was required to place the withdrawn money in an interest-bearing account, resume depositing his salary into the joint account and transfer another $20,000. He was also directed to restore Sarah's access to their financial accounts.
Sarah subsequently alleged that Charles had issued three cheques totalling $19,400 after depositing the additional money. She also complained that he had again restricted her access to the joint account.
Charles admitted during the trial that he had stopped depositing his salary into the account around May 2024 and again around February 2025. He also acknowledged removing Sarah as an authorised credit-card user, saying her spending exceeded what he could afford.
Court rejects request to postpone trial
In October 2025, Sarah sought $30,000 towards expert assistance and legal expenses, saying she needed professionals to examine her husband's assets.
The final hearing was scheduled for December 8, 2025. Three days before the trial, she sought a postponement, saying she could not afford a forensic accountant and had recently discovered a bank account and credit card for which she had not received records.
The trial judge rejected the request, noting that the divorce case had been pending since February 2024.
The appeals court upheld that decision. It said Sarah had raised the need for expert assistance in October but waited until shortly before the hearing to seek a postponement. Her lawyer had also failed to explain what an accountant might discover or how the findings would affect the case.
Medical businesses should be included 
The main issue in the appeal was Charles's ownership interests in Baldwin Bone and Joint, a surgery centre and other medical consulting businesses.
During the trial, Sarah submitted an assessment estimating that Charles's 15.38% interest in Baldwin Bone and Joint Medical Center, LLC, was worth $219,491. The calculation was based on a September 2025 balance sheet.
The lower court admitted the document but treated the business as Charles's separate estate. It also declined to accept a tax document relating to the surgery centre as a valuation. Charles had invested $150,000 in that centre but maintained that its shares were "worth nothing" because the business was operating at a loss.
The appeals court found that the business interests had been acquired during the marriage. Charles completed his medical training seven years after the wedding and purchased his medical-practice partnership interest in 2020 or 2021. There was no evidence that he had acquired these interests before marriage or received them through gifts or inheritance.
Under the law, property accumulated during marriage can form part of the marital estate. The appeals court said the lower court had no sufficient evidence to classify the businesses as Charles's separate property.
Charles argued that the lower court had already accounted for the investments through a $70,000 property settlement awarded to Sarah. However, that payment covered several matters, including retirement-account adjustments, moving expenses and his violations of earlier court orders.
The lower court had neither valued the businesses nor specified how much of the settlement was intended to compensate Sarah for them. The appeals court therefore found that the payment did not correct the error in excluding the businesses from the marital estate.
Home, vehicle and alimony issues
The appeals court also addressed the couple's marital home. The lower court had recorded its equity as $100,000, describing the figure as an agreement between the parties. Sarah disputed this and argued that the equity was $150,000, based on a $1.5 million appraisal and a $1.35 million mortgage.
The appeals court found no clear agreement on the amount and directed the lower court to determine the equity from the evidence.
It also ordered the lower court to consider the Mercedes G-Wagon, which had been excluded because it belonged to an LLC, alongside the valuation of the business interests.
The court left the decision not to award Sarah a vehicle unchanged because she had testified that she did not hold a valid driving licence at the time of the trial.
It also allowed the lower court to reconsider alimony after completing the revised property division, as the two issues are connected.
The appeals court upheld the refusal to postpone the trial and the decision not to hold Charles in contempt or impose additional sanctions.
It ultimately reversed the division of marital property and sent the case back to the Baldwin Circuit Court. The lower court must now value the medical-business interests, include them in the marital estate and reconsider an equitable division of the couple's assets.

title: Could IShowSpeed have a future beyond YouTube? Usain Bolt weighs in after surprising 100m performance
text:
IShowSpeed has made a name for himself as one of the most popular YouTube streamers, but could he also have a future in professional sports? The internet star recently got the chance to show his running skills in front of eight-time Olympic champion 
Usain Bolt
. During their latest meeting, Speed ran the 100-meter race in an impressive 10.352 seconds. His performance caught attention, and Bolt was seen reacting positively to the result. The moment has now started conversations about Speed's future in sprinting.
IShowSpeed clocks an impressive 10.35 seconds in 100m race in front of Usain Bolt
The 100-meter race took place in IShowSpeed's November 22, 2026, YouTube video titled 
"I RACED USAIN BOLT!" The video is part of the second season of his series called Speed Goes Pro. In this series, Speed gets help from famous athletes as he tries to learn their sports and improve his skills.
IShowSpeed ran the 100 meters in 10.352 seconds in the video. That is a solid time for someone without track experience. It takes a lot of strength and training to achieve that.
He got to train with Usain Bolt this time. Bolt is the fastest man in the world and holds the 100-meter world record at 9.58 seconds. He also has 8 Olympic gold medals.
The timing got people talking right away. Some viewers began wondering if the YouTube star could do more than entertain people online.
Could Usain Bolt's advice help IShowSpeed become a professional sprinter?
One of the biggest highlights of the video was Usain Bolt's reaction to Speed's performance. The Olympic legend seemed impressed by his run and acknowledged that the streamer could have the potential to become a professional sprinter.
A speed comparison graph shared after the race also revealed an interesting detail. IShowSpeed recorded a higher speed in miles per hour than Bolt during the first 15 meters of the sprint. This suggests that Speed showed strong acceleration at the start of the race.
However, this does not mean Speed was faster than Bolt over the entire 100 meters. Bolt still holds the world record of 9.58 seconds and has years of professional sprinting experience.
For Speed, getting praise from someone like Bolt is still a big moment. It also gives him a chance to learn from one of the greatest runners in history.
In the end, IShowSpeed's 10.352-second run has given fans another reason to talk about his athletic skills. Whether he chooses to follow professional sprinting in the future remains to be seen, but his latest performance has certainly caught the attention of the sporting world.

title: Kick streamer CostaKid sparks controversy after attacking woman in viral livestream clip
text:
Kick streamer CostaKid has become the subject of online criticism after a video showed him getting into a physical fight with a woman during a livestream. The incident reportedly took place inside a car after the woman poured water over his head. CostaKid, 20, quickly turned around and reacted angrily. The video shows him throwing an object at her, spitting on her, grabbing her hair and hitting her several times. The incident has sparked a debate about his violent reaction.
CostaKid attacks woman after she pours water over his head during livestream
The incident happened while CostaKid was livestreaming from inside a car. According to reports, the woman poured water over his head as a prank. However, the streamer did not take it well and quickly lost his temper.
After the water was poured on him, CostaKid turned around and started fighting with the woman. He reportedly threw something at her before spitting on her and grabbing her by the hair. The video then showed him hitting her several times.
People who were present during the incident could be heard shouting at CostaKid and asking him to stop. However, the fight quickly became the main topic of discussion after the clip started spreading on social media.
The video has drawn strong reactions from viewers. While some people have pointed out that pouring water on someone without their permission was wrong, others believe that CostaKid's physical reaction was far too extreme.
Kick streamer CostaKid faces backlash after viral fight with woman
Following the incident, CostaKid has faced criticism from people discussing the video online. Many viewers have questioned his actions and believe that the woman pouring water on him did not justify the way he reacted.
The incident has also brought attention to the streamer's previous legal trouble. According to a report, CostaKid was arrested in Miami the previous month and charged with aggravated assault with a deadly weapon.
CostaKid is a 20-year-old streamer from Suffolk, England. He has gained more than 500,000 followers across platforms such as TikTok, Kick and Instagram.
The latest livestream incident has added to the attention surrounding his online activities. Some viewers have also questioned whether he could face further legal trouble following the fight. However, there is no confirmed information about any new arrest or charges related to this incident.
For now, the viral clip continues to attract attention, with viewers debating the actions of both people involved. While the water prank may have upset CostaKid, his reported physical response has become the biggest talking point.

title: Why did a small GTA 6 streamer break down in tears after Ibai Llanos joined his Twitch stream?
text:
A small streamer named Dicrim_RD69 had an emotional moment after Twitch star Ibai Llanos joined his GTA 6 livestream and helped him reach thousands of viewers. The Dominican streamer had been playing the game with almost no one watching when Ibai discovered his broadcast on November 19. After joining the stream, Ibai asked his followers to visit the channel, follow Dicrim and keep him company. The shoutout quickly changed the stream, bringing in more than 3,200 viewers within hours.
How did Ibai Llanos help a GTA 6 streamer go from zero to over 3,200 viewers?
Dicrim_RD69 was streaming GTA 6 when Ibai Llanos came across his broadcast. At that time, the small streamer had no viewers watching him. Ibai joined the livestream and simply wrote,
"Hello."
However, Ibai did much more than just visit the channel. He shared Dicrim's stream with his followers on social media and asked them to visit, follow and spend some time with the small creator.
The response was much bigger than Dicrim could have expected. His viewer count quickly increased and reached 3,243 people within a few hours. For a streamer who was used to playing in front of almost nobody, seeing thousands of people watching him was an unforgettable moment.
Dicrim became emotional when he saw the sudden support. He thanked Ibai and said that he had been a fan of the Spanish streamer for a long time. He also told the viewers, 
"You guys have brought me to tears."
Why did the small GTA 6 streamer get emotional during his call with Ibai?
During a video call with Ibai, Dicrim explained that he had been streaming for more than a year but had struggled to attract viewers. He said that playing and streaming without anyone to talk to sometimes made him feel sad. He was especially upset the night before Ibai found his channel.
Dicrim also shared that his family could not afford video games when he was younger. This made the moment even more special for him, as he finally had thousands of people watching him play a game he enjoyed.
Ibai understood how Dicrim felt because he had also started small. He remembered that when he was 14, he used to stream basketball commentary with his cousin. Just like Dicrim, they also had no viewers at the beginning.
Ibai encouraged the young streamer to continue doing what made him happy. He told Dicrim,
"If it makes you happy, keep doing it."
The advice came from someone who had experienced the same struggle before becoming a major name in online streaming.
In the end, Dicrim's story became a reminder that even a small act of support can make a big difference to a new creator. Ibai's visit gave him a huge audience, but it also made him feel that his hard work had finally been noticed. For Dicrim, the day was about much more than reaching 3,243 viewers; it was about feeling supported after a long time of streaming alone.

title: Alaska Supreme Court upholds $3,780 child support after dentist understated income
text:
A financial disclosure that initially resulted in a father’s monthly child support payment being less than $700 became the focus of a legal fight over income transparency and parental responsibility. A dentist in Alaska claimed his earnings were $36,960, but it turned out he was making substantially more, which led to a dramatic hike in child support payments for his four children. The Alaska Supreme Court has now upheld the new order, ruling that parents cannot take advantage of protections against retroactive child support changes to benefit from knowingly underreporting their income.
Legal dispute over income difference
According to the Alaska Supreme Court’s decision in Bowen v. Ray, 2 No. S-18430 (Nov. 20, 2026), Doug Bowen is a pediatric dentist and member of the Alaska Army National Guard who separated from his wife, Deana Ray, in March 2022. Two months later, Ray filed for divorce.
During the course of the proceedings, both parties submitted financial information to determine child support. Bowen reported earning $36,960 a year. In January 2023, the Palmer Superior Court ordered Bowen to pay $697.94 a month for their four children, who are mostly in Ray’s care.
But Ray later disputed the calculation, saying Bowen had not included several sources of income in his financial disclosures.
Documents reveal substantially larger earnings
In describing the proceedings, the Alaska Supreme Court said Ray submitted tax documents showing Bowen earned about $183,688 from his private dental practice in 2021. She also submitted employment records indicating he started with Southcentral Foundation in September 2022 with an annual salary of about $176,000.
The higher-paying employment was supported by Bowen’s own testimony at the divorce trial. His pay records showed gross monthly earnings of about $13,266, plus a $17,247 sign-on bonus.
The lower court also considered business deductions claimed by Bowen, among them accelerated depreciation. It found the deductions were not enough to justify discounting his much higher income in setting child support.
Increase in monthly payments for back pay
In September 2023, the Superior Court found that Bowen's income exceeded the applicable Alaska child support guideline amount of $126,000. This increased his monthly obligation from $697.94 to $3,780 effective October 1, 2022, when he had started his higher paying job.
Bowen appealed, claiming the increase violated Alaska Civil Rule 90.3, which generally bars retroactive changes in child support obligations.
The Alaska Supreme Court rejected that argument, noting that the restriction was not intended to protect people who knowingly misrepresent their financial circumstances.
Supreme Court dismisses retroactivity argument
In a Nov. 20, 2026, decision, the Alaska Supreme Court ruled that the state’s restrictions on retroactively changing child support do not extend to instances of intentional financial misrepresentation.
The judges said the original order was based on misleading income information and allowing the lower payment to stand would undermine the purpose of child support protections. The court noted the rules were designed to ensure children receive appropriate financial support and not to shield parents who knowingly provide false financial disclosures.
The Supreme Court therefore affirmed the lower court’s decision to apply the higher payments as of October 2022, when Bowen began his higher-paying job.
Property dispute adds another dimension
The appeal also concerned Silver Springs, a commercial property legally owned by Bowen’s parents, which they purchased for his dental practice.
The lower court determined that during the marriage, Bowen had been paying his parents about $2,000 each month, with the understanding that eventually he would own the property.
Bowen argued the payments were for rent and other unpaid debts, but the Alaska Supreme Court ruled there was enough evidence to support the lower court decision that payments had created an equity interest in the marital estate.
The judges therefore agreed with the ruling that that equity was to be treated as marital property subject to division in the divorce.
Earlier support adjustment separate
The Alaska Supreme Court also noted a later order, issued in February 2024, lowered Bowen’s monthly child support obligation to $1,562.81 after a change in the custody arrangement between the parents. But that adjustment wasn’t included in the appeal.
The state's highest court, in its final ruling on the matter, upheld the lower court's conclusions on the divisions of marital property and the child support computations, leaving unchanged the decisions that were contested.

title: Welsh glamping-site owner faces £135,000 legal bill over disputed driveway
text:
A Welsh glamping site owner has been ordered to pay £135,000 in legal costs after a dispute over whether her neighbours can drive past their front door to reach their own parking space. Carol Esteban is now challenging the ruling at the Court of Appeal, according to AOL and The Independent.
The case centres on a shared track at Cwmtawe Farm near Abercrave, close to the Brecon Beacons. Esteban argued that the neighbours’ right of way ended opposite their front door, while Neil and Nadine Gould said it extended far enough for them to park beside their home.
How the dispute began
The Goulds’ detached cottage, Cwmtawe Villa, is surrounded by land belonging to Cwmtawe Farm, where Esteban runs a glamping site across more than 60 acres. The properties were once held by the same owner, but the villa was sold off in 1949 and the original documents have been lost.
A 1964 conveyancing document gave the villa’s owners an easement, allowing them to use the farm track on foot or by vehicle. The problem was that the map attached to that document was missing the letter B, which was meant to mark where the right of way ended. Esteban argued that the right of way stopped at the front door of the villa. 
The Goulds argued that it extended a few feet further, allowing them to turn into the hardstanding parking area beside their house.
What the court decided
In July 2025, Judge Milwyn Jarman ruled in favour of the Goulds. He found that their vehicular right of way extended to the space on the north side of the villa, where they currently park.
The judge rejected Esteban’s argument that the right of way should stop at the front door. He said that interpretation would lead to impracticality, since the Goulds would be able to drive up to the door but not park or turn around. The court also ordered Esteban to pay £135,000 in legal costs. That figure has now become part of the appeal.
Why the appeal matters
Esteban’s lawyers argue that the High Court judge did not properly interpret the 1949 conveyance. They say the judge instead decided what the parties should have agreed to, rather than what the documents actually said, as per the reports. They also argue that there is no evidence the track extended beyond the front door of Cwmtawe. The appeal focuses on whether the easement stops at the front door or allows the Goulds to reach their parking spaces.
Esteban’s legal team also challenges the costs order. They point out that she succeeded on parts of her counterclaim, including a finding that a waterpipe had been installed unlawfully on her land.
What the neighbours say
The Goulds’ lawyers argue that the judge reached the right conclusion. They say the easement must allow the couple to reach their parking spaces, otherwise it would have little practical use.
They argue that the layout of the land shows there is no physical feature stopping the Goulds from driving onto their parking area. The lawyers say the judge’s interpretation gives practical effect to what the original grantor intended.
The appeal judges have reserved their decision. The outcome will determine whether the Goulds can continue using the track to access their parking space, and whether Esteban will have to pay the £135,000 costs bill.

title: South Carolina woman fears 2 highway routes could take her home and son's house
text:
A proposed $1.56 billion highway extension in South Carolina has left a homeowner worried about the future of her family after two possible routes were found to pass through her house. Jenny Cooper, who lives in Juniper Bay outside Conway, said the proposed alignments could force her family off their property, with one of the routes potentially wiping out her son's house as well. The project, intended to improve traffic movement and connectivity across Horry County, has triggered concerns among residents over potential displacement, property loss and environmental damage. Cooper said she understands why a new highway is needed but fears that rising property prices could make it difficult for her family to find another place where they can continue living together.
Two proposed highway routes could pass through South Carolina homeowner's house
Cooper raised her concerns during a public meeting at the Horry County Government and Justice Center, where residents gathered to discuss plans for the SC-22 highway extension.
According to WPDE, she said two of the proposed routes could pass directly through her home in Juniper Bay. The possible alignments have raised questions about what would happen to families whose houses and land fall within the proposed corridors.
Cooper is particularly concerned about the impact on her son's property. She explained that one possible route could cut through their land, potentially leaving her son's house directly in the path of the proposed highway.
"Where this land is or this road's coming through, it's going to cut our land in half. So, my son's house will be completely took out if it goes that direction," Cooper said.
She also expressed concern about finding another property where she, her son and his family could continue living together, particularly as land prices continue to rise.
What is the $1.56 billion South Carolina highway project?
The proposed development is an extension of South Carolina Highway 22, also known as SC-22. Previously referred to as the Southern Evacuation Lifeline, the project is intended to improve transportation connections in Horry County and surrounding areas.
The approximately 28-mile extension is planned to connect US Highway 501 near Conway with US Highway 17 in the Murrells Inlet area, close to the Horry-Georgetown county line.
Officials have described the project as a way to reduce traffic congestion, improve access to essential services and provide another connection across the Waccamaw River. Hurricane evacuation has also been cited as one of the potential benefits.
The estimated cost of the wider project is approximately $1.56 billion, including construction and environmental mitigation. However, the project remains in the planning and environmental review stages.
Three possible routes remain under consideration
The highway extension has undergone several rounds of route assessments. Officials initially examined 22 potential alignments before narrowing the options through subsequent screening.
Three alternatives, identified as Routes 2, 3 and 4, remain under consideration.
The proposed alignments cover different parts of Horry County:
- Alternative 2: Covers the Juniper Bay and Singleton Crossroads areas.
- Alternative 3: Passes through the Timberlake area.
- Alternative 4: Covers the Guiton Crossing area and passes near St. James High School.
The alternatives have generated concerns among residents who fear losing their homes, farmland and other parts of their properties if a particular alignment is selected.
Residents of The Farm at Timberlake have also raised concerns about Alternative 3, which could potentially affect dozens of homes in the neighbourhood.
Environmental concerns surrounding the proposed highway
The highway proposal has also attracted opposition from environmental campaigners concerned about its potential impact on the Waccamaw River region and nearby protected habitats.
One of the major concerns involves the Waccamaw National Wildlife Refuge, which protects wetlands, bottomland hardwood forests and habitats used by numerous wildlife species.
Environmental advocates have warned that highway construction could disturb natural habitats, affect wetlands and waterways, and fragment wildlife corridors. They have also raised concerns about potential effects on water quality and flood-prone areas.
The US Army Corps of Engineers is overseeing the federal environmental review process, which will examine the potential consequences of the proposed alternatives.
Residents and environmental organisations have argued that the project's impact on surrounding communities and ecosystems should be carefully considered before officials select a route.
Environmental campaigners question highway's evacuation purpose
The project's earlier name, Southern Evacuation Lifeline, has also become a point of disagreement between officials and environmental advocates.
State and county officials have described the highway as potentially useful during hurricane evacuations. However, Amy Armstrong, who leads the South Carolina Environmental Law Project, questioned whether the proposed road would effectively serve that purpose.
According to WPDE, Armstrong said the Army Corps of Engineers had previously rejected the project's description as an evacuation route.
She argued that the highway would eventually connect with US Highway 501, where motorists could encounter significant traffic congestion.
The Corps has identified reducing traffic congestion and improving access to services on both sides of the Waccamaw River as key objectives of the project.
Officials say no final route has been selected
Horry County officials have stressed that the proposed alignments are still being evaluated and that no final decision has been made.
Thomas Bell, the county's public information director, acknowledged that homeowners could become concerned when they see maps showing potential highway routes passing through their properties.
He said the maps were being presented to inform residents and gather their feedback rather than indicate that a particular route had been approved.
The Army Corps of Engineers is also considering public comments as part of its environmental review. Residents have been encouraged to share concerns about property impacts, environmental consequences and other aspects of the proposal.
The Corps is expected to prepare a Draft Environmental Impact Statement as the review progresses, followed by another opportunity for public feedback.
The project is currently projected to move towards construction around 2030, with completion targeted around 2035.

title: Seattle man loses nearly $4 million debt relief after hiding $39,600 inheritance
text:
A Seattle man lost more than $3.9 million in bankruptcy discharge after a court found that he had concealed inheritance rights and an interest in a business. The Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Washington entered judgment revoking Nevin Middleton’s Chapter 7 discharge on October 20. As a result, Middleton remains liable for his debts, and creditors may pursue payment from him after the case is closed.
According to the US Department of Justice, he had received about $39,600 from his father’s probate estate but failed to disclose the inheritance and business interest in his bankruptcy filings. The ruling followed a trial victory by the Justice Department’s US Trustee Program (USTP), which had sought to revoke the discharge over those undisclosed funds.
Middleton’s failed construction business led him to seek bankruptcy relief
Middleton first filed an individual Chapter 11 reorganisation case to address debts arising from a failed custom home construction business. The case was later converted to a Chapter 7 liquidation. In April 2024, he received a Chapter 7 discharge covering $3,967,997 in unsecured debt. Most of that amount involved claims brought by creditors who had invested in his projects.
The discharge had been granted in April 2024. The court’s later decision revoked that relief after finding that Middleton had obtained it through fraud. 
The ruling means the debts were no longer discharged, and creditors are free to seek payment from him once the bankruptcy case is closed.
Middleton disclosed his $39,600 inheritance months after receiving debt relief
Several months after receiving the discharge, Middleton appeared at an evidentiary hearing concerning his claim to a homestead exemption on some of his real estate. During that hearing, he disclosed for the first time that he had received two deposits from his late father’s probate estate. The distributions totalled about $39,600 and had been paid after he filed for bankruptcy but before he received the discharge.
The money went into a business bank account that Middleton controlled. However, his original bankruptcy schedules and statements did not list his inheritance rights or his interest in the business connected to the account. The disclosure came only months after the discharge was granted.
US Trustee Program took Middleton to trial over undisclosed inheritance
The US Trustee Program’s Seattle office investigated the undisclosed funds. Investigators found that Middleton had instructed his sister, who was the executor of their father’s probate estate, to send the distributions to a business account. The private trustee administering Middleton’s bankruptcy case did not know of that business account.
At trial on the US Trustee Program’s complaint seeking revocation of the discharge, Middleton gave a different explanation for the money. He testified that the payments were loans from his sister. The bankruptcy court considered the evidence before reaching its decision. It concluded that Middleton had knowingly and fraudulently failed to report the funds to the Chapter 7 trustee. The court also found that he had obtained his discharge by fraud.
Court ruling leaves Middleton responsible for his debts
The Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Washington entered judgment on October 20, revoking Middleton’s Chapter 7 bankruptcy discharge.
With the discharge revoked, Middleton remains liable for his debts. Creditors are free to pursue payment from him after the bankruptcy case is closed. USTP Director Stephen V. Falanga said, “The bankruptcy discharge is the key to a fresh start, but debtors must be transparent about their financial affairs to receive it. The USTP remains steadfast in its commitment to protect the integrity of the bankruptcy system from dishonest debtors.”
Disclaimer: This article is based on the US Department of Justice’s announcement regarding the Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of Washington’s judgment revoking Nevin Middleton’s Chapter 7 bankruptcy discharge. The Times of India has not independently verified the details of the bankruptcy proceedings or the findings reported by the court.

title: Yorkshire woman grows 4,200 trees inspired by grandchildren's climate protests
text:
A woman in her 80s from North Yorkshire has grown more than 4,000 trees and donated them for planting in several nature reserves. Janet Willoner began growing trees from seed in 2019, after her grandchildren joined Fridays for Future climate demonstrations. Inspired by her grandchildren’s love of nature, she collected seeds from lanes near her home and raised the trees herself. Her project has since expanded, with thousands of saplings donated for planting elsewhere. According to BBC News (2025), her trees have gone to Knaresborough Forest Park and Yorkshire Wildlife Trust reserves. Willoner estimates she has grown about 4,200 trees and raises around 800 annually. She hoped to reach 5,000 in 10 years.
How did Janet begin growing thousands of trees in her garden
Willoner started growing trees in 2019, when her grandchildren joined the Fridays for Future climate demonstrations. Their involvement and their love of nature inspired her to find a practical way to help the environment. She initially thought planting trees would be too difficult, so she began collecting seeds instead. The seeds came from lanes around her home in Boroughbridge, North Yorkshire.
She first managed to grow 400 trees but kept the project private until she knew it was working. Willoner said, "I didn't tell anyone what I was doing because I thought if they don't grow, I shall look very silly."
The project later expanded into a long-term commitment, with trees donated for planting in other places across the region.
Her homegrown trees have reached several nature reserves
Six years after she began, Willoner estimated that she had grown around 4,200 trees as of 2025. She has given the young trees to several organisations so they can be returned to nature. The destinations include Knaresborough Forest Park, Yorkshire Wildlife Trust reserves and Make it Wild, a community interest company that works to regenerate landscapes in North Yorkshire.
Willoner estimates that she grows about 800 trees each year, with a variety of species among them as of 2025.
She described the project as something that had become a "way of life" and said she found it "hugely inspiring".
What inspired Janet to keep growing trees
When she began the project, Willoner set herself a target of growing 5,000 trees over 10 years. The target is not necessarily an endpoint. Willoner said, "The trouble is, I don't think I can stop. I think even when I get to 5,000 there's quite a big possibility that I'll keep going. You don't need a degree in order to grow trees, anybody can do it who has got the time and the interest and the commitment."
In 2020, Make It Wild received 300 of Janet’s first seedlings for planting on its nature reserves in Nidderdale, marking the start of a friendship and an idea, according to Make It Wild.
Janet received recognition for her tree-growing efforts
Willoner's efforts have also brought recognition beyond the organisations receiving her trees. She has been nominated in the Green category of BBC Radio York's Make a Difference Awards. Despite the nomination and the scale of the project, she has no plans to put away her gardening gloves.
She described the work as hugely inspiring and said it had become part of her everyday life. Reflecting on the wider crisis, she said, "I felt the human race is in a crisis at the moment, but from any crisis there's the opportunity for something better or different to emerge from it."
Her continued work is focused on raising trees and donating them for planting elsewhere in the region, rather than stopping after her target.

title: Southern African pythons use attractive tail movements to lure prey
text:
Southern African pythons have been observed using an unusual tail movement to lure potential prey, revealing a hunting technique that had never been formally recorded in the species. The finding grew out of research that combined historical records with social media observations. Videos and photographs posted by members of the public helped scientists identify previously overlooked aspects of the snakes' behaviour, including a specialised hunting method that offers a fresh insight into how these large reptiles capture food.
Southern African pythons use tail movements to attract prey
The behaviour, known as ‘caudal luring,’ involves a snake moving its tail in a way that resembles something attractive to potential prey. Rather than moving its entire body, the python remains still and uses the tip of its tail to draw an animal closer. The research documenting this behaviour was conducted by Kirsty J Kyle and Colleen T Downs from the University of KwaZulu-Natal in South Africa and published in the journal 
African Zoology
 on 8 May 2025.
The researchers described one observation they made on a medium-sized southern African python, measuring between 1.5 and 2 meters. The snake was kept in captivity for a short period before being released and the unusual behavior was observed while it was in a large glass enclosure.
According to the study, domestic chickens were moving freely nearby when the python adopted an ambush position. It then began moving the visibly marked end of its tail in a repeated, wave-like motion.
One of the chickens noticed the movement and approached the tail from several metres away. Throughout the encounter, the python kept the rest of its body completely still, continuing to move only the tip of its tail.
The glass enclosure prevented the chicken from becoming a meal, but the researchers considered the behaviour a likely attempt to attract prey. The observation provided the first documented evidence of caudal luring in southern African pythons.
Why is the python's tail important in this technique
The study explains that southern African pythons have a distinctive colour pattern towards the end of their tails. While the upper surface continues the camouflage pattern found across the rest of the body, the underside has prominent black and white markings.
This contrast makes the tail tip particularly noticeable when exposed and moved. The researchers suggested that the combination of its colouring and movement could help attract animals within striking distance.
Caudal luring is not entirely new to science. Some other snake species are already known to use their tails to attract potential prey. However, the behaviour had not previously been formally documented in southern African pythons.
The researchers also noted that these snakes were already known to use their tails defensively. Photographs and videos collected through social media showed individuals displaying their tails when threatened by predators. The new observation suggested that the same distinctive tail features could serve more than one purpose.
Social media helped scientists understand python behaviour
The discovery formed part of a wider investigation into the feeding habits and hunting strategies of southern African pythons. In their study, Kyle and Downs combined information from historical scientific literature with observations collected from social media platforms.
The researchers examined Facebook, YouTube, Instagram and iNaturalist, looking for photographs and videos showing the snakes feeding or interacting with potential prey. They collected records posted up to 1 May 2024 and manually checked the material to identify the snakes and their prey as accurately as possible.
The social media investigation produced 238 feeding observations. Of these, 219 could be identified to species level, giving researchers a wealth of information about the python’s diet.
Facebook accounted for 84.5% of the collected social media records, while YouTube contributed 6.3%. Instagram and iNaturalist provided the remaining observations.
What did the study reveal about the python's diet
The investigation found that southern African pythons consume a much wider variety of animals than earlier records suggested. The researchers identified 104 vertebrate species eaten by the snakes.
These included 36 mammalian species, 41 bird species and two reptilian species in the social media records, alongside additional prey identified through other sources.
They also found that the python’s food preferences seem to change as it grows. Smaller individuals were more often recorded eating birds, and larger snakes were more often associated with mammals.
Among the recorded feeding incidents involving pythons measuring less than 1.5 metres, 89% involved birds. In comparison, birds accounted for only 6.1% of the feeding records involving the largest snakes, which measured more than 3 metres.
Records of mammalian prey were especially common for impala, with 44 incidents identified in the study. But they said that bigger pythons may be more able to take on larger mammals because they provide a bigger meal.
What do the findings mean for future python research
The study also highlighted how southern African pythons adapt their hunting strategies to the availability and behaviour of prey. Some individuals were repeatedly observed using the same trees and locations to catch birds.
One python recorded through a live webcam was seen on 9 occasions taking different birds from the same branch of a dead tree. Another was observed visiting the same tree in a residential area over 7 months, where it fed on 6 different bird species. These observations suggested that the snakes could make use of locations where potential prey regularly gathered rather than relying entirely on chance encounters.

title: Kerala's Sneha Joy lost polls by 13 votes in 2020; now, she has won a Rs 32 crore lottery in Canada
text:
In 2020, Sneha Joy from 
Kerala
's Ernakulam district contested the local body elections as a United Democratic Front (UDF) candidate but lost by 13 votes. Little did she know that a new beginning was waiting for her. She moved to Canada and five years later she won the Canadian $5 million lottery jackpot, which is nearly Rs 30 crore! Sneha, a woman from Kerala's Ernakulam district, won in Canada’s Lotto 6/49 lottery, turning an ordinary lottery ticket into a life-changing windfall.
Let’s find out more about this lucky woman:
Meet Sneha Joy
Sneha is originally from Vengoor near Perumbavoor in Kerala. Her journey from local politics to becoming a millionaire in Canada has made headlines. While her electoral debut did not go as she had hoped, she got lucky thousands of kilometres away.
Before moving to Canada, Joy had built an academic and professional career in Kerala. An engineering graduate with a triple-main degree, she worked at a firm in the Special Economic Zone (SEZ) in Kakkanad, Ernakulam.
In 2020, she decided to enter electoral politics and contested the Vengoor Grama Panchayat elections as a UDF candidate from the Kaippilly ward. 
But she lost to her rival from the Left Democratic Front (LDF) by just 13 votes.
Four months after the election, Joy married Vijil Varghese, an engineer from Nilambur in Malappuram district. The couple moved to Canada and settled in Edmonton.
A routine lottery check changed everything
According to a report by Onmanorama, Joy had purchased her ticket through the Lotto Spot app and checked it after the October 21 draw. She had matched all six numbers in the Classic jackpot of Canada's Lotto 6/49 lottery.
The six winning numbers were:
1, 10, 18, 22, 33, 37
The numbers that changed her life as Joy had won CAD 5 million. She had become a multi-millionaire overnight.
"I was shocked!" she said while claiming the prize.
She summed up her emotions in three words: "Shock. Happy. Relief."
The jackpot was officially confirmed by the Western Canada Lottery Corporation (WCLC) on November 20. The lottery corporation announced Joy as the winner of the CAD 5 million prize.
Paying off her mortgage is her first priority
"I'm going to pay off my mortgage," she said, explaining that becoming free of her home loan is the main priority.
For many families, owning a home comes with years of loan repayments, monthly installments and financial planning. Joy's decision to use her unexpected fortune to settle her mortgage reflects the importance she places on financial security.
Once that responsibility is taken care of, she hopes to fulfil another dream: travelling around the world.
"After that, I'm going to take a trip around the world!" she said.
She also intends to share a portion of her winnings with her family.
"To be financially stress-free!" was how she described the best part of winning the jackpot in her conversation with lottery officials.
The WCLC release also recorded her intention to help her family, suggesting that the windfall is not just about personal ambitions but also about sharing the benefits with those closest to her.
A new life in Canada
Her father, PP Joy, is a local Congress booth president, while her mother, Joly, is a homemaker. Sneha is their only daughter. Her connection with public life was perhaps not surprising, given her father's involvement in local politics.
Her marriage to Vijil Varghese came four months after the election. The couple subsequently relocated to Edmonton, Canada, where they began building a life together.
Five years later, the woman who once came tantalisingly close to winning a local election in Kerala has found herself celebrating a much bigger and entirely unexpected victory in a different country. For a family from a modest agricultural background, the news of their daughter winning millions in Canada is undoubtedly a moment to cherish.
And while a lottery jackpot can change someone's life overnight, Joy's first thoughts after the win have been about clearing her home loan, travelling the world and sharing her happiness with family, plans that make this unexpected fortune all the more relatable.

title: Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan seeks execution delay, says he was defending Taliban
text:
Fort Hood shooter Nidal Hasan has asked a federal court to delay his scheduled execution, saying he intends to argue that he was defending the Taliban from an unlawful US military attack.
In a court filing signed by Hasan on Tuesday, he said he intended to demonstrate that the military court’s judgment and his death sentence had been obtained and were being maintained in violation of his federal constitutional and statutory rights.
The filing could delay the Trump administration’s plans to execute Hasan on December 3. A hearing has been scheduled for Wednesday morning.
Hasan, who is representing himself with assistance from lawyers at the American Civil Liberties Union’s Capital Punishment Project, said he intended to continue representing himself in the legal fight.
Hasan wants to revive defence barred at trial
One of Hasan’s central arguments is that he was prevented from presenting a defence that his actions were legally justified because he was trying to protect the Afghan Taliban from what he described as an unlawful attack by the US Army.
Hasan had argued that he was acting in “defense of others”, according to court documents. However, the military judge barred him from presenting that argument during his 2013 trial.
After dismissing his lawyers and choosing to represent himself, Hasan largely remained silent during the three-week trial. 
While the military called nearly 90 witnesses, Hasan called none in his defence and made no closing argument.
A military jury found him guilty of multiple counts of murder and attempted murder for the shooting, which left 13 people dead and 32 wounded.
The case has been assigned to US district judge Tony Mattivi in Kansas, where Hasan is being held at the military prison at Fort Leavenworth. Mattivi was nominated by president Donald Trump and confirmed by the Senate in June.
What happened in the Fort Hood attack?
On November 5, 2009, Hasan walked into the Soldier Readiness Processing Center at Fort Hood, Texas, where soldiers were waiting for medical tests and preparing for deployment.
He opened fire with a handgun fitted with laser sights, killing 13 people and wounding more than 30 others.
Hasan was shot by law enforcement officers during the attack, leaving him paralysed from the waist down and confined to a wheelchair.
He was convicted by a military jury in 2013 of 13 counts of premeditated murder and 32 counts of attempted premeditated murder. The jury sentenced him to death.
Execution controversy and survivors’ objections
Trump authorised Hasan’s execution on the recommendation of defence secretary Pete Hegseth. The execution, scheduled for December 3 at Fort Hood, would be the first US military execution by firing squad since World War II and the first military execution since 1961.
The plan drew controversy after Hegseth announced that the execution would be public and the Pentagon confirmed it would be livestreamed. Critics from both parties raised concerns that broadcasting the execution could fuel radicalisation and turn it into a spectacle.
Trump later said the execution would not be livestreamed, but that immediate family members of the victims could witness it in person if they chose.
The latest court filing comes amid further dispute over who will be allowed to attend. Military officials have denied requests from three survivors of the 2009 shooting to witness the execution, citing regulations, security and space constraints.
The survivors argued that the military should recognise them as victims under a broader definition that includes direct physical, emotional or financial harm. The Army rejected their appeal, saying regulations specify who may attend a military execution.

title: Australian family finds 5-foot venomous snake inside their toilet
text:
An Australian family was shocked to discover a five-foot venomous red-bellied black snake emerging from their toilet after it squeezed its way through a narrow sewerage pipe. The 1.5-metre reptile had travelled through a pipe measuring just 50mm in diameter before appearing in the bathroom of a home in Rossmore, southwest Sydney. The family called local snake catcher Daniel May to remove the unexpected visitor. However, the rescue proved unlike anything he had experienced in his career. In an interview with 7News, Daniel May, a professional snake catcher, described the incident as “pretty phenomenal”, revealing that the snake was in such poor condition that he took it into his care.
Snake catcher stunned by giant snake found in Australian toilet
May told 7NEWS the snake was unusually large and strong enough to travel through a pipe measuring around 50mm in diameter. Describing the incident, he said: “It was quite a big, chunky and strong snake; even the pipe he swam up was only about 50mm wide so you got to think it was a pretty tight squeeze for him to get up through there and make his way into the toilet.”
He also described the unusual rescue as “pretty phenomenal”. According to May, the family was surprised when the snake appeared in the toilet bowl. He suggested they had been trying to chase it away before realising where it had emerged.
Australian snake catcher nurses exhausted toilet snake back to health
Despite years of attending calls to remove snakes and other reptiles from homes and businesses across Sydney, May said he had never personally dealt with a similar incident before. Although he had heard of snakes entering toilets in other areas, this was the first time he had encountered one during a rescue.
“I’ve seen people post about it. You hear about it a lot in the country and stuff like that ... but that’s the first time, myself, that I’ve had it happen,” he told 7NEWS.
The snake was in poor condition after travelling through the sewerage pipe. May said it appeared to be seriously affected by the journey and “looked like it was going to die”. Rather than immediately relocating it, he decided to take it into his care until it had recovered sufficiently to be released.
May and his wife monitored the red-bellied black snake over the following couple of days, checking that it was not injured and had regained its strength. They planned to release it on Wednesday, October 21, after allowing it time to recover.
Snake catcher warns Sydney residents as snake calls surge
May also warned that snake encounters were becoming more frequent across Sydney as temperatures began to rise ahead of summer. He said he was receiving as many as six calls a day to catch and remove snakes, with that number expected to reach 10 calls daily in the following weeks.
He explained that snakes emerge from their winter hibernation and enter their breeding season, making them more active as they search for mates. “They do a lot more travelling this time of year,” May said, adding that they also ventured through backyards more frequently than usual.

title: Watch: Armed men hold 30 hostage in Colombia supermarket; 10 rescued
text:
At least 20 people remained hostage at a supermarket in Colombia's Cartagena on Tuesday by armed men, following a failed attempt to hijack an armoured cash van, President Abelardo De La Espriella and national police said.
The hostage-takers had released 10 people from the store, which belongs to the Exito chain, Reuters reported.
The armed men reportedly took the hostages after police responded to their failed attempt to intercept an armoured vehicle carrying cash from a shopping mall, De La Espriella said. They subsequently barricaded themselves inside the supermarket in Cartagena's La Castellana neighbourhood.
Images shared on social media earlier on Tuesday appeared to show people kneeling against the supermarket's windows with their hands seemingly tied. However, they couldn’t be verified.
Heavily armed military personnel and police officers were deployed outside the store. Police said on social media that all available human, technological and specialised resources had been mobilised to protect those still inside and secure their safe release.
"All of our human, technological, and specialised resources are deployed, under interagency coordination, to protect the citizens who remain inside the store and secure their safe release," the police said, as per Reuters.
Authorities did not immediately disclose the identities of the hostage-takers or those being held. De La Espriella assured the public that the hostages would be freed.
"I guarantee the Colombian people that we will free those people," he said during a visit to Villavicencio, where an overnight car bombing had taken place. The government blamed the bombing on a group of dissidents from the former Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) who rejected the 2016 peace agreement.
The Exito chain said the safety and protection of people was its priority and that authorities were handling the situation at its Cartagena store.
Meanwhile, Cartagena's Rafael Nunez airport resumed flight arrivals after a suspension of around 45 minutes. The armed forces had used one of its runways in connection with the hostage situation.

title: What is the Fifth Amendment, and why is Trump urging Jensen Huang not to invoke it
text:
US president Donald Trump has urged Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang to tell the truth when he faces congressional questioning next week. Adding that he does not believe the chipmaker’s head needs to invoke the Fifth Amendment over his alleged links to a woman suspected of having connections to Chinese intelligence.
Trump also said he was open to granting Huang a presidential pardon if necessary, but did not think such a step would be required.
Asked in an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday whether he would consider pardoning Huang over potential crimes, Trump said, “It’s always an option, I guess, but I don’t think it’ll be necessary.”
“I don’t think he needs to take the Fifth. I think it’s an interesting story for people,” Trump said, adding that he wanted Huang to “just tell the truth”.
Trump said he had always found Huang to be “100% aboveboard” and described him as a “very smart person”, while acknowledging that the Nvidia chief’s lawyers would have to advise him on how to approach the questioning.
What is the Fifth Amendment?
The Fifth Amendment to the US Constitution protects individuals from being compelled to give testimony that could incriminate them in a criminal case.
The protection is commonly known as the right against self-incrimination. 
When a person refuses to answer a question on this basis, the act is often described as “pleading the Fifth”.
The amendment forms part of the Bill of Rights, ratified in 1791, and also includes protections against double jeopardy, guarantees of due process and limits on the government’s power to take private property without just compensation.
Invoking the Fifth Amendment is a constitutional right and does not, by itself, establish guilt, but it does create a sense of doubt surrounding the innocence. Whether Huang chooses to invoke it during congressional questioning would be a decision made with advice from his lawyers.
Why is Jensen Huang facing scrutiny?
Huang is expected to testify before US lawmakers in relation to questions about Nvidia’s business dealings with China and compliance with American export restrictions on advanced artificial intelligence chips.
The scrutiny has also centred on Huang’s relationship with a Chinese woman suspected by US intelligence officials of having links to Chinese intelligence. Huang has acknowledged having an affair with the woman.
Lawmakers are also expected to examine allegations that Nvidia chips may have been diverted to Chinese AI companies through third countries, potentially circumventing US export controls.
According to CNN, Huang is scheduled to testify behind closed doors before a US Senate committee on Tuesday next week, followed by a public hearing on Friday.
The hearings are expected to focus on Nvidia’s export practices and the national security implications of its business dealings with China.
Nvidia’s board has also reinstated Huang as chief executive, following his removal from the position less than two weeks earlier. Trump had claimed credit for persuading the board to bring Huang back.

title: 6 missing after Cessna plane crashes off Mississippi coast in US
text:
A search operation is under way off the coast of Mississippi after a Cessna aircraft carrying six people, including two children, crashed near Horn Island on Tuesday. The US Coast Guard has deployed rescue teams to locate those on board, but no passengers had been found as of the latest update.
The Coast Guard said it received information about the crash from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), following which crews began searching the waters northeast of Horn Island.
“@USCG rescue crews are searching for a downed Cessna Centurion 210 aircraft with 6 people, 2 mi NE of Horn Island, Mississippi, after @USCG watchstanders in Mobile received a report from @FAANews, Tuesday,” US Coast Guard Heartland said in a post on X.
The aircraft reportedly went down southwest of Pascagoula at around 3.30pm (local time), an FAA spokesperson told Fox News Digital. The spokesperson, however, said the number of people aboard had not been confirmed.
"The number of people on board is unknown at this time," the spokesperson said, adding that the FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) would investigate the crash.
Local media reports cited by Fox News suggested that four adults and two children, aged between eight and 12, were travelling on the aircraft. 
The plane was reportedly descending at nearly 10,000 feet per minute before it went down.
The Cessna Centurion 210 was flying from New Orleans Lakefront Airport to Page Field in Fort Myers, Florida. It disappeared from FAA radar at around 3.45pm local time.
As the search continued, Coast Guard personnel recovered parts of the aircraft, including its cabin, along with a life raft and three life jackets. WLOX reported that no one aboard had been located by around 5.40pm.
The operation involves multiple agencies, including the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources and the Jackson County Sheriff's Office, NBC News reported.
Rescue crews are focusing on waters roughly two nautical miles northeast of Horn Island, a barrier island in the Gulf Coast region that is designated as a wilderness area and can only be reached by private boat.
The NTSB has confirmed that it is aware of the incident and is collecting information. It will lead the investigation, working with the FAA, to establish what caused the aircraft to crash.

title: Two arrested after masked men break into Prince William and Kate’s country home
text:
Two men have been arrested on suspicion for breaking into Prince William and Kate Middleton’s country home, Anmer Hall, in Norfolk on Monday.
The men were arrested on suspicion of burglary and trespass, according to The Times. Police said the estate was unoccupied at the time of the break-in. The suspects remain in custody.
Anmer Hall, a 10-bedroom Georgian house on the Sandringham Estate, is used by the Prince and Princess of Wales as a country retreat. The couple often spend weekends and holidays there with their three children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis.
The property also holds personal significance for Catherine, who recuperated there following surgery and cancer treatment in 2024.
The house was built in 1802 and became part of the Sandringham Estate in 1896, when it was purchased by the future King Edward VII. It was later leased to several members of the British aristocracy, including the Duke and Duchess of Kent.
William and Kate’s move to Anmer Hall was confirmed in 2013, following their marriage and the birth of Prince George. The couple moved in two years later after a major renovation, which reportedly cost around $2 million and included improvements to the house and measures to increase privacy.
The property has since served as a family retreat, including during the Covid-19 lockdown. The Prince and Princess of Wales now spend most of their time at Forest Lodge in Windsor, while continuing to use Anmer Hall as a country escape.

title: Israel govt formation: Eisenkot, Lieberman join hands in bid to oust Netanyahu
text:
Former Israeli military chief Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party agreed to a coalition pact with Avigdor Lieberman's right-wing opposition party on Tuesday, marking the first such alliance since last month's election.
Yashar said Eisenkot met Lieberman, head of the Israel Our Home party, and the two agreed on a deal following their discussions, Reuters reported.
Efforts to form a government without Prime Minister 
Benjamin Netanyahu
 are gathering pace.
The Knesset was sworn in on November 10 without a new government in place, after the October 27 vote cost Netanyahu his majority but left his rivals without a clear route to power. President Isaac Herzog has asked Eisenkot to form a government, while Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister.
Eisenkot has until December 6 to assemble a government under his 28-day mandate, with the option of a 14-day extension. Should he fail, Netanyahu will get a chance to try, and if neither succeeds, Israel will go to another election next year, Reuters reported.
Netanyahu's Likud alliance with far-right and ultra-Orthodox parties secured 53 of the 120 Knesset seats, short of a majority of 61. Eisenkot's centre-right Yashar and its potential partners, Lieberman's party among them, hold 48.
Arab parties, which have 19 seats and share Eisenkot's opposition to Netanyahu, could give his bloc a path to a majority.
Yashar and Israel Our Home won 21 and seven seats, respectively. The deal comes despite Lieberman's earlier objections to a government reliant on Arab party support or to joining a unity government with Netanyahu. Lieberman has repeatedly said his main goal is to remove Netanyahu from power.
Talks are also under way between Eisenkot, some members of the so-called change bloc and Likud on a possible unity government. Separately, the left-wing Democrats party, which holds eight seats, announced it was suspending negotiations with Eisenkot, citing his progress in talks with Likud and a stalemate in efforts to form a change government. Party leader Yair Golan has said he favours a government without Netanyahu that includes Arab parties.

title: Flights delayed at Chicago O’Hare airport as ground radar system suffers outage
text:
Flights bound for Chicago’s O’Hare International Airport were briefly grounded on Tuesday after an outage of the airport’s ground radar system. The disruption to traffic came during the Thanksgiving holiday rush, delaying many passengers.
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) lifted the ground stop after a short while, transitioning to a ground delay programme before cancelling it later in the day. Flights are still facing delays, with the FAA warning that another ground stop could be imposed if congestion builds up on runways and taxiways.
The outage was believed to be linked to the ASD-X ground surveillance radar system, which tracks aircraft and vehicles on airport runways and taxiways to help prevent collisions.
The FAA said technicians were working to repair the equipment. At one point, delays for flights headed to O’Hare were averaging 47 minutes, while the airport’s arrival capacity had been reduced to 72 flights an hour from its usual 100.
About 350 flights, or 12% of traffic, had been delayed earlier in the day, with most of the affected flights bound for Chicago. Flight-tracking site FlightAware later reported around 400 delayed arrivals and departures, including delays caused by other factors.
The FAA also warned of a shortage of air traffic controllers at Chicago’s Terminal Radar Approach Control centre from 8.30 pm, which could further affect traffic in the region.
Tuesday’s disruption marked the second ground stop at O’Hare this week. Flights were halted on Monday because of staffing issues at the Chicago TRACON.
Nearly 1.67 million passengers are expected to pass through O’Hare over the seven-day Thanksgiving travel period, up 7.2% from 2025.

title: West Virginia town sues to save 12 historic buildings from demolition in national park
text:
A historic railroad town in West Virginia has asked a federal judge to stop the National Park Service from demolishing 12 buildings inside New River Gorge National Park and Preserve. The town wants the court to act before demolition crews arrive on 30 November. The Town of Thurmond and the New River Gorge Historical Society filed a lawsuit on 18 November in the US District Court for the Southern District of West Virginia, according to the West Virginia Record. The case names the National Park Service and Eric G. LaPrice, the park's acting superintendent, in his official role.
The dispute centres on a $36 million project funded through the Great American Outdoors Act. The project aims to improve facilities and restore parts of the former coal mining town. However, federal spending records cited by the West Virginia Record show that about $750,000, or roughly 2 per cent of the total budget, has been set aside for demolition. The 12 buildings due to be removed include houses and outbuildings in Thurmond, the Prince Brothers General Store in nearby Prince, and a building used to store pool chemicals at Camp Brookside.
Legal claims over preservation and review rules
In their lawsuit, the town and the historical society accuse the National Park Service of breaking three federal laws: the Administrative Procedure Act, the National Environmental Policy Act and the National Historic Preservation Act. They are not seeking financial compensation. Instead, they want the court to declare that the agency has acted unlawfully and issue an order stopping the demolition until it completes further reviews. They also want officials to consider other options, including allowing private groups to lease and restore the buildings.
"Plaintiffs do not ask the court to substitute its judgment for NPS's," the complaint states, as reported by the West Virginia Record. "They ask the court to require NPS to honor its own plans and agreements, and to follow federal law, before taking irreversible action."
Thurmond was once an important railway centre for West Virginia's southern coal industry. Its historic district was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1984. The lawsuit argues that plans to demolish the 12 buildings go against earlier National Park Service documents. These include a 1992 development plan for Thurmond, a 2011 general management plan and a 2022 survey of historic buildings and other resources. According to the plaintiffs, the 2022 survey found that most of the buildings examined in Thurmond had retained their historic character and needed only basic maintenance. They claim the Park Service failed to carry out the necessary repairs and later used the buildings' poor condition as a reason to demolish them.
Disputes over consultation and bridge weight limits
The lawsuit also claims that the National Park Service broke a preservation agreement signed in February 2025. The agreement required the agency to consult formally with Thurmond and other interested groups before moving ahead with demolition. Under the agreement, the Park Service had to share draft demolition plans and schedules, allow consulting groups 30 calendar days to send comments, and explain how it had considered their feedback.
Thurmond officials say they were never given a complete set of demolition plans. According to the West Virginia Record, the lawsuit states that the Park Service sent out a significantly changed schedule on 13 November, only two days before the agency said the period for submitting comments would end. Local officials have also questioned whether the town's roads and bridge can safely handle the heavy equipment needed for the work. The lawsuit raises concerns about the impact of demolition machinery and lorry traffic on roads maintained by the town. It also points to the 10-tonne weight limit on the only bridge leading into Thurmond.
Questions over private leasing alternatives
Another major part of the case concerns whether the Park Service properly considered leasing the buildings to private groups instead of demolishing them. The plaintiffs say the agency initially rejected this option because the park did not have enough staff, funding or a suitable programme to manage leases. However, a later agency decision allowed some buildings to remain if suitable lease proposals were received. The town and the historical society argue that the Park Service has not explained why the same option was not considered for the 12 buildings now facing demolition. The agency issued a request for lease proposals on 13 November, but none of the 12 buildings listed for demolition were included, according to the complaint.
Broader $36 million restoration plans
The National Park Service approved its revised demolition plan in July 2025. Court documents cited by the West Virginia Record show that the agency accepted that demolishing the buildings would cause lasting damage to the historic district.
